correctness.rationale: Independently integrated on the barycentric difference domain: in two coordinates the overlap density of the difference w with sum w_i=0 is 2(1−sum max(w_i,0))² on sum max(w_i,0)≤1. In each of the six sign sectors the square-distance polynomial is x u²+y v²+(x+y−z)uv for the two incident sides x,y at the isolated-sign vertex and the opposite side z; the Jacobian is one. The beta integral of u^p v^q(1−u−v)² over u,v≥0, u+v≤1 is 2p!q!/(p+q+4)!. The exact independent replay (python3 /workspace/branches/independent_triangle.py) gives coefficients 1/18 and 1/60 on pure degree-one and degree-two monomials, zero mixed degree-two coefficient, and coefficients 23/4200, 7/4200, −28/4200 on the cubic pure, mixed squared-linear, and xyz patterns respectively. The inverse elementary symmetric formula and side-side-side congruence establish injectivity. The two explicit triangles are strict for the stated small r, share m1 and m2, have |Δm3|=r³/420 and ordered squared-side discrepancy r. For the uniform bound the coefficients are Lipschitz in the bounded input moments, so on the boundary of any cluster of radius-η disks about the first roots the original polynomial modulus is at least η³; choose η comparable to δ^(1/3), with a generic slightly larger radius if disks are tangent. Rouché preserves multiplicity in each cluster, with diameter at most 6η; a real matching bounds ordered discrepancies as well. At δ=0 the cubics agree, and for large δ the root bound suffices. The example rules out all larger exponents near equilateral. The result concerns squared sides and population moments, not a sampling theorem.
